To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the light-dependence can be used to scale-up phototrophic bioreactors of different types, (ii) the light-dependency changes significantly when irradiation is dynamically changing, (iii) the maximum growth rates are doubled when irradiation changes dynamically, but (iv) tolerance of microalgae against high irradiances is drastically reduced.

light-dependent growth kinetics can be transferred from small-scale flat-plate gas lift photobioreactors to large-scale thin-layer cascade photoreactors, but that light-dependent growth kinetic parameters have to be determined under dynamic light conditions to predict microalgal growth in dynamic day-night climates.

the light-dependent growth rates of microalgae can be transferred from small to large scales if the mean light availabilities are kept constant and that light-dependent growth kinetics are different under dynamic irradiation conditions compared to constant conditions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the transfer of light-dependent growth kinetics between different scales and different reactor types.
the transfer of growth kinetics from one scale to the other and the influence of different irradiation regimes (constant vs. dynamically varying) on the growth of two Nannochloroposis strains.

the development of a light-dependent growth model for the prediction of the growth of N. salina and N. gaditana under different light conditions and different reactor scales, which is an important step towards a more efficient scale-up and scale-down of phototrophic cultivation processes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the light-dependence and tolerance of microalgae should be determined with the same light regime as applied in the respective photobioreactor.
light-dependent growth kinetics are transferable from one reactor type to another only if the same irradiation is applied.
light-dependent growth kinetics can be successfully transferred from small to larger scales if irradiation is constant and the mean light availabilities are comparable.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the transferability of the light-dependent growth kinetic of microalgae is dependent on the light regime and reactor type.
the transfer of light-dependent growth kinetics between different reactor types is possible if the microalgal suspensions in the different reactors are exposed to similar light conditions.

the transfer of light-dependent growth kinetics is possible from small to large scale for photobioreactors with constant LED irradiance, but that the transfer of the same kinetics to dynamic conditions is not possible without further investigations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the mean light availability is a suitable parameter for scaling phototrophic growth in different types of reactors.
the mean light availability in the suspension can be used to scale up light-limited microalgae growth, but not for growth with fluctuating irradiation.
growth of N. gaditana 1.99 and N. salina 40,85 in flat-plate gas lift photobioreactors with LED illumination can be scaled to thin-layer cascade reactors.
